post.title: The December 11 THCA Ban: What Lost THC Can't Sell After It
post.excerpt: On December 11, 2026, federal hemp rules start counting THCA and capping products at 0.4 mg of THC per container. Every product Lost THC sells today is over that line. That ends our vapes, pre-rolls, gummies and brownies, and restocks are already shrinking before the date.
post.author: Lost THC
post.content:
Short answer: The federal hemp ban reaches THCA on December 11, 2026. On that date the federal definition of hemp starts counting THCA as THC and caps finished products at 0.4 milligrams of THC per container. Every product Lost THC sells today is far over that cap, including our THCA, THCP and CB9A vapes, our THCA pre-rolls, our gummies and our brownies. Unless Congress changes the law before then, we can't keep selling the current lineup after December 10. Until then we are restocking less often and in smaller amounts, so strains and sizes will sell out and may not come back.

For the statute itself, quoted line by line, see our guide to the 2026 hemp law.

The Two Hemp Ban Dates in 2026

Section 781 of Public Law 119-37, signed in November 2025, rewrites the federal definition of hemp. It was set to take effect on November 12, 2026. In September 2026, H.R. 6500 split that date in two:

Date What takes effect Effect on Lost THC
November 12, 2026 The ban on products containing cannabinoids the cannabis plant cannot produce naturally. None for most products. THCA, THCP, delta-8 and delta-9 all occur naturally in the plant. The open question is CB9A, used in our 7G CB9A Live Resin, 8G CB9A V2 and 2G THCP (see below).
December 11, 2026 Total THC including THCA, the 0.4 mg per container cap, and the rule on naturally occurring cannabinoids made outside the plant. Every current product line falls outside the federal hemp definition.

Section 2019 of H.R. 6500 says that "until December 11, 2026," section 781 applies only to the products described in the two clauses for cannabinoids "not capable of being naturally produced" by the plant (H.R. 6500, enrolled). The enacted text sets no later date. As of October 8, 2026, December 11 is still the date.

Where CB9A fits

Our 7G CB9A Live Resin and 8G CB9A V2 disposables use CB9A, and the 2G THCP blends it with THCP. As our CB9A explainer covers, sellers describe CB9A as made in a lab, and there is no agreed chemical structure in public sources. As of October 8, 2026, no federal regulator has said whether CB9A counts as a cannabinoid the plant "cannot produce naturally." If a regulator decides it does, the ban reaches these three products on November 12 instead of December 11. We will update this page if that changes.

What We Won't Be Able to Sell After December 11

The new cap is 0.4 milligrams of THC per container, and it counts THCA plus other cannabinoids. That means our 8g device will have to be reduced 20 times!

Product line Main cannabinoids Example strength After December 11
THCA disposables: 2G, 3G Diamond, 5G Switch, 7G Live Resin, 8G V2 THCA, some with THCP and delta-8 3G Diamond: 3,000 mg THCA diamonds Ends
THCP disposables: 3G Diamond, 5G Switch, 2G THCP, delta-8, THCH; the 2G also has CB9A 2 to 5 grams of extract per device Ends
CB9A disposables: 7G Live Resin, 8G V2 CB9A, THCP 8G V2: 8 grams of extract Ends, and could end Nov 12 (see above)
THCA pre-rolls: Moonrock, Hash Hole, Flawless Blend, diamond-infused THCA flower plus concentrate 2G Moonrock: 650 mg THCA Ends
Gummies: Exotic Blend, Exotic 2ct THCA, delta-9, THCP; the 2ct is delta-8, THCP, delta-9 1,500 mg per gummy Ends
Brownies: Chocolate and other flavors Delta-9 and CBD 150 mg delta-9 per brownie Ends
Bundles Mixes of the above Several devices or bags Ends

A new formula wouldn't get around the cap.  The law also removes naturally occurring cannabinoids that were "synthesized or manufactured outside the plant" (sec. 781), which covers delta-8 made from CBD. Our delta-8 vs. delta-9 vs. THCA guide explains how each one is made.

Why Stock Is Getting Tighter

Nobody can sell what is left on the shelf on December 11, so manufacturers and distributors are winding down now. Ours are making fewer runs, and at least one hemp company has stopped production altogether: an Associated Press report published by Spectrum News in October 2026 says a Wisconsin THC beverage maker has halted production.

For you, that means:

  • We are still restocking, but less. Restocks are smaller and further apart than they were earlier this year.
  • Sold out may mean gone. When a strain, size, or flavor sells out, there may not be another batch before December 11.
  • Your usual strain may not be available. Our disposable comparison and sativa vs. indica guide can help you pick something close if your favorite is gone.

What to Do Before December 11

  • Don't wait for the last week. Orders need time to ship and arrive before December 11. We haven't set a final order date yet. When we do, we will post it on this page.
  • Check your state's law. Some states already restrict THCA before the federal change. We don't ship to Alaska, Arkansas, Hawaii, Idaho, Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota, New York, Oklahoma, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah or Vermont. See is THCA legal in your state.
  • Buy only what you expect to use before the deadline. We can't advise on keeping product after December 11. Federal and state possession rules are a question for a licensed attorney in your state.
  • Watch for fakes. Other sites already sell counterfeit Lost THC vapes. Our guide to spotting a fake Lost THC vape shows what to check, and lab reports for our products are on our COA page.

Could Congress Still Change It?

It could, but no law has passed that does. The industry is lobbying for a regulated market in place of a ban, and the AP reports that hemp companies have offered their own limits: a 21-and-over age requirement, a cap on THC per package and a ban on imported cannabis compounds. The same report cites a Whitney Economics estimate that the ban could cut retail revenue by $28.3 billion and displace about 225,000 jobs.

The December 11 date has already moved once, and it could move again. Plan as if it will hold. If the law changes, we will update this page and our law guide as soon as we confirm it.

What the Ban Doesn't Change

  • Dispensaries. State-licensed medical and adult-use dispensaries sell under state marijuana law, not the federal hemp definition. If your state has a licensed program, those stores keep selling after December 11.
  • Drug tests. A drug test looks for THC metabolites and can't tell a legal product from an illegal one. THCA turns into THC when you heat it, so the ban changes nothing about how a vape or pre-roll shows up. Our drug test guide covers detection times.
  • CBD. CBD doesn't get you high, so it doesn't count toward the 0.4 mg cap. Full-spectrum CBD products also contain some THC, and that THC does count.
  • Stricter state laws. A state that already restricts THCA keeps its own rules, and states can ban more than federal law does.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is THCA getting banned?

At the federal level, yes, unless Congress acts. From December 11, 2026, the hemp definition counts THCA toward total THC and caps finished products at 0.4 mg per container. A THCA vape, pre-roll, or gummy can't meet that limit, so it falls outside the hemp definition. Federal law treats cannabis that isn't hemp as marijuana.

When does the hemp ban start?

In two steps. Products with cannabinoids the plant cannot produce naturally lose hemp status on November 12, 2026. The THCA, total-THC and 0.4 mg rules start December 11, 2026.

Can I still buy from Lost THC before December 11?

Yes. We are selling and shipping as normal, with smaller and less frequent restocks. Order early, because sold-out items may not return. Our CB9A products could end sooner if regulators decide CB9A is not a natural cannabinoid.

Will Lost THC keep selling anything after December 11?

Not our current lineup. Every product we sell today is over the 0.4 mg cap. If Congress changes the law, or we add a product that meets it, we will announce it on this page and by email to our customers.

What about my rewards points or store credit?

Use them before December 11, while the current lineup is still for sale.

How will I know if the date changes?

We will update this page when a change becomes law. You can check any hemp bill yourself on Congress.gov, which lists each bill's text and whether it has passed.

Does the ban affect delta-9 gummies and brownies too?

Yes. The cap applies to each container. One of our brownies has 150 mg of delta-9, and its whole package can hold only 0.4 mg.

Will there be a sale before the ban?

As we approach the date, whatever stock is left will go on a flash sale; until then, our Current prices are in our shop.
